title: rand-engine adopts the dadaia-workspace specs pattern v9; the v1 law files are replaced by the v9 scaffold
context: The repo carried a dadaia-workspace pattern v1 specs tree (commit cd7cd12), below the oldest upgradable version, so `specs init --replace-foreign` scaffolded v9 (operator, 2026-10-03). The onboarding commit replaces AGENTS.md and specs/AGENTS.md, which the pre-push law-deletion check (dadaia-workspace ADR 0151 M3) refuses unless a cited accepted ADR rules it.
decision: We adopt specs pattern v9 as rand-engine's specs canon. The v1 AGENTS.md and specs/AGENTS.md are replaced by the v9 scaffold; the old tree is not kept in the working tree and stays readable in git history at cd7cd12. Release 0.7.0 is the first live release under v9.
consequences: + backlog, bugs, releases and memory follow the workspace lifecycle. - v1 notes are only in git history.
measured_by: .dadaia/.venv/bin/dadaia doctor reports no TREE- or LEDGER-ADR-SCHEMA finding for rand-engine; git show cd7cd12:specs/constitution.md exits 0

title: Relations are stateless key columns: pk/fk column methods computed from the seed and the row index; the SQLite/DuckDB checkpoint and the global NumPy seed are deleted
context: 0.6.4 links PK and FK through a process-global SQLite/DuckDB checkpoint read inside a wall-clock watermark: integer FKs come back as bytes, a PK does not make rows unique, db_checkpoint is a no-op, the spec loses `constraints` after one batch, FK correctness depends on scheduling and no key crosses a process (audit 0.6.4, D1-D4, D16, D19). The seed is process-global (np.random.seed), so constructing a generator resets the caller's NumPy state and two generators interfere (D13). TPC-H/DS, PDGF and dbldatagen v1 derive keys from the row index instead. Operator grill 2026-10-03, D1-D5. Operator rulings on SPEC 0.7.0 rc-1, 2026-10-03: permuted keying by pk kwargs only; one `skew` kwarg; event-time ordering backlogged.
decision: We will declare relations as two column methods in the RandSpec grammar: `pk` (style `sequence` = start + i*step, or `permuted` = a bijection of the row index over a declared domain, depending only on `domain` and an optional `key`, never on the generator seed; an optional `format` renders either as a string; random-digit keys are rejected) and `fk` (kwargs `parent` = the parent's pk column spec, `parent_size`, `skew` = 0 uniform or > 0 Zipf over permuted ranks; it picks a parent index from the generator seed and the child row index and rebuilds the parent key, never looking it up). A pk value is a pure function of its kwargs and the row index; an fk value of the parent definition, the generator seed and the row index; a stream's microbatch continues the row index. We delete the `constraints` spec key, ConstraintsHandler, the SQLite/DuckDB/base handlers, db_checkpoint, the reset_checkpoint option and the duckdb dependency. Each generator owns one np.random.default_rng(seed), passed to the core as `rng`; no module touches the global NumPy state. SparkGenerator rejects pk/fk in 0.7.0.
consequences: + PK unique by construction, FK always hits, FK in the parent PK set for any parent and child seeds (seed=None included), identical keys for any chunking and across processes, no database, no clock; ~370 LOC and one runtime dependency leave. + The caller's NumPy state is never touched. - Breaking: `constraints`, db_checkpoint and option leave; same-seed values differ from 0.6.x (constitution invariant 4 revised by SPEC 0.7.0 rc-1). - Spark has no keys until a parity release; time-ordered streaming relations (the watermark's intent) are not offered.
measured_by: `git grep -nE 'np\.random\.seed|ConstraintsHandler|db_checkpoint|reset_checkpoint|duckdb' -- rand_engine pyproject.toml requirements.txt` prints nothing; `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_8_consistency.py` passes its default contract cases at <= 10^4 rows (PK unique at 10^4 rows, every FK in the parent PK set for int and string keys, 1 batch vs N stream microbatches identical, spec unchanged after get_df); `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -m stress tests/test_8_consistency.py` passes the same contract at 10^6 rows in the CI stress job; and `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_2_data_generator.py` passes its rng cases (np.random.get_state() unchanged, same seed same frame, generators independent)

title: Direction: the speed niche on a single NumPy/Arrow node; rows per microsecond first, SparkGenerator gets nothing new, no new runtime dependency, a 1M/10M benchmark row and seeded goldens before any method
context: The operator ordered this record on 2026-10-24: "ADR para as regras; aprovo apagar os 4 métodos". The rulings are the 2026-10-11 direction rulings, confirmed on 2026-10-24 ("Confirmo todas (Recomendado)"), and the north star "Velocidade e nicho (Recomendado)" (grill handoffs 2026-10-24T160915Z roadmap and 2026-10-24T170504Z rc-2). The forces: (1) adoption is small, so effort must go where the library can win: 1 GitHub star, 0 open issues, 26 PyPI downloads in 2026-08 and 80 in 2026-09 (pypistats, mirrors excluded; GitHub API; read 2026-10-24, roadmap-backlog handoff 2026-10-24T161601Z). (2) Spark costs more than it returns: 9 of the 61 archived bugs have component core/_spark_core.py, and one more is in the Spark validator (specs/bugs/_archive/bugs_histo.jsonl); four methods, SparkCore.gen_distincts_map, gen_distincts_multi_map, gen_distincts_map_prop and gen_complex_distincts, return NULL columns with only a warning. (3) Speed is measured, and the output path is the slow part: in CI the column methods run at 7-512 rows/µs, but CSV writes at 3, Parquet at 2.4, JSON at 0.5 and stream_dict at 0.17 rows/µs; an embedded transformer is 86x slower at 1M rows, and stream_dict defaults to 5.0 records/s. (4) The direction had no record: from 2026-10-11 the rulings lived only in the operator's ruling record, until candidate 0.8.1 rc-2 J1.T1 wrote them into the constitution as ## Direction (a056299). Threshold (specs/ADRs/AGENTS.md §1): one-way door, because the four Spark methods are deleted and a spec that ran now raises, and twelve months of work are committed to one engine; architecturally significant, because it fixes the engine topology, the runtime dependency surface and the entry bar for every new method or key; and three genuine options exist.
decision: We make rand-engine, for twelve months from 2026-10-24, the fastest Python generator of related synthetic data on a single node, NumPy and Arrow: a declarative spec becomes pk/fk tables, then files and streams. We measure speed ("velocidade") in rows per microsecond, the mean of a measured run; speed comes first, then resource efficiency. We put the NumPy single-node engine first; SparkGenerator gets nothing new. We add no new runtime dependency. We land no new method or key without a benchmark row at 1M and 10M rows. We run benchmarks only in CI. We touch a generation method only after seeded golden tests pin its values. We keep local tests light, as specs/memory/QUALITY.md ## Test architecture states.
consequences: + One home per rule: the rules live in specs/constitution.md ## Direction and are not copied into the QUALITY.md or ARCHITECTURE.md ## Principles. + The four Spark NULL methods are deleted and refused at validation (candidate 0.8.1 rc-2, Job 3), which closes the Spark surface that bred 9 archived bugs and removes the dead bodies. + Every new method arrives with a measured 1M/10M row and a seeded golden, so a slowdown or a changed seeded value fails before merge. + The dependency surface stays numpy, pandas and pyarrow, with faker optional. - Spark users get nothing new: no keys, no seeded ordinary columns and no new methods on SparkGenerator, and a spec that used the four NULL methods now raises. - Features outside the niche wait: no new built-in sinks or engines (sinks come as docs recipes). - Speed claims hold on the CI runner only, since benchmarks are not run locally. - Resource efficiency is reported (peak MiB per row) but never gated. The native core under the Python API is a later 2.0 path ("1.0 cedo; núcleo nativo = 2.0"), not an option rejected here.
measured_by: No new runtime dependency: pytest tests/test_9_cli.py::test_pyproject_declares_open_python_and_the_four_dependencies (pins the [tool.poetry.dependencies] dict exactly, the optional faker entry included, so a new dependency or extra fails), and pytest tests/integrations/test_public_api.py::test_wheel_requires_only_open_floors_of_the_three_core_dependencies (wheel core Requires-Dist is exactly numpy, pandas, pyarrow). A 1M/10M benchmark row and speed in rows/µs: pytest tests/test_benchmarks.py::test_benchmark_inventory_covers_every_numpy_catalog_method tests/test_benchmarks.py::test_committed_benchmark_artifact_has_every_inventory_row_at_1m_and_10m, and the CI job 'Stress tests and speed benchmark' (.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml, PRs to development and master), which times every row at 10^6 and 10^7 as rows/µs over the mean (benchmarks/speed.py) and fails a row slower than 1.3x its base. Seeded goldens: pytest tests/test_2_data_generator.py -k golden (every NumPy method but pk/fk has a seed-42 SHA-256 golden). Spark refusal of the four NULL methods: pytest tests/test_1_common_validator.py -k refuses_correlated_methods_on_spark. Partial checks: the 'or key' half of the benchmark-row rule has none, since speed.MODIFIERS is a pinned literal (tests/test_benchmarks.py:85), not derived from the keys the validator accepts; the goldens omit pk/fk and every Spark method. No mechanical check yet: the north star; 'SparkGenerator gets nothing new' beyond the four refusals (test_validator_tables_match_engine_maps_and_signatures derives the Spark set from METHOD_CATALOG, so a new Spark method passes); 'then resource efficiency' (peak MiB is reported, never gated); 'benchmarks run only in CI' and 'local tests stay light' (pyproject.toml addopts -m 'not stress' and tests/AGENTS.md:17 are configuration and law; no test fails on a violation).

options.name: (A) The speed niche on a single NumPy/Arrow node (chosen)
options.tradeoff: All effort goes to rows/µs on one engine and the slow output path; the Spark NULL methods are deleted; Spark and broad-surface users get nothing new.

options.name: (B) Multi-engine parity, Spark first-class
options.tradeoff: Spark users would get keys, seeded columns and the four correlated methods; reaches cluster-scale users.
options.rejected_because: Spark already holds 9 of the 61 archived bugs with four methods still returning NULL, every feature would be built and debugged twice, and at 26-80 monthly downloads the cost has no measured demand behind it; the operator ruled "Velocidade e nicho (Recomendado)" and "Nada além disso (Recomendado)" for Spark.

options.name: (C) A broad feature surface: new sinks and engines
options.tradeoff: More integrations (Kafka, S3, databases, new engines) as built-ins; wider first-look appeal.
options.rejected_because: Each sink or engine adds runtime dependencies and a new bug surface while output writing is already the slowest path (CSV 3, Parquet 2.4, JSON 0.5 rows/µs against 7-512 for columns); the operator ruled "Nenhum novo; receitas (Recomendado)" for sinks.
